title: SiST: Token Similarity and Sparsity Aware Optimization for Transformers on FPGA
problem: Transformer inference on resource-constrained FPGAs is expensive due to high computational cost in QKV generation, attention, and FFN modules.
motivation: Prior FPGA work focuses on attention computation, but QKV generation and FFN typically dominate overall cost; sparsity and token patterns offer optimization opportunities.
method: SiST combines cross-stage sparsity prediction before QKV generation with token similarity-based clustering in FFN and weight sparsity exploitation, supported by hardware architecture handling unstructured sparsity.
key_novelty: Holistic algorithm-architecture co-design exploiting both token similarity and sparsity across all three transformer modules on FPGA.
limitations: Accuracy loss <2% but not detailed per-layer; cross-stage sparsity prediction requires offline weight clustering.
primary_theme: Sparsity and token similarity optimization for FPGA transformers
